- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early-to-mid forecast horizon; adjust upward by 3–8% for 30-day forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model overreacts and overshoots, then fails to correct — reduce forecast by 5–10% after peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts drift upward over time despite persistent downward trends in true prices — apply downward momentum correction.
- Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast curve forward by 1–2 days for better alignment.
- In periods of high volatility (e.g., 2024-05), model fails to capture extreme swings — add volatility buffer (±5–10%) to forecast range.
